newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Euro-shares follow Wall St bull, dlr steady.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Euro-shares follow Wall St bull, dlr steady.

text.p: European shares rose on Thursday morning after Wall Street put a week of declines behind it and surged overnight, while the dollar was steady.
"The Dow's raging bull may be back on track," the head of share trading at a large investment bank in London said. "People will be pretty confident now -- until Wall Street falls again."

London's FTSE 100 index was up 12.8 points, or 0.3 percent, at 4,220.3 at midday, while in Paris the CAC 40 index was up 31.26 points, or 1.27 percent, at 2,496.27. In Frankfurt the DAX was up 12.35 points, or 0.41 percent, at 3,011.55.

In New York on Wednesday the Dow industrial average, which had fallen during the previous five sessions, closed 84.66 points higher at 6,740.74, its best gain since January 3 when it surged 102 points.

But gains in the broader U.S. share markets were negligible and U.S. analysts said the market's extreme volatility, a growing worry, had prompted investors to seek the relative safety of big-name blue-chip stocks.

Volatility was the watchword in Tokyo, too, where the key Nikkei average ended with a loss of 2.57 percent, or just over 471 points. it gave back almost half of the gains racked up in the previous two sessions.

European dealers said participants on both sides of the Atlantic would remain cautious ahead of next week's U.S. Federal Reserve regular monetary meeting on February 4 and 5, which could change U.S. interest rates.
While most economists did not expect the Fed to push up U.S. rates, some believed signs of a robust U.S. economy would lead to a tightening sooner rather than later.
Higher interest rates would sorely test the world's share markets, many of which are at or near record levels, by making returns on alternative investments and cash more attractive.
The underlying caution was reflected in mediocre trading volumes in London, Europe's biggest share market.
"We may not get a Fed (interest rate) hike next week but the market knows the rate cycle has changed and that higher rates are just around the corner," one London trader said.
French shares were particularly strong, hitting a new trading record and briefly breaking through the psychologically-important 2,500 level.

"The (corporate) results have been taken very well, Wall St looks good, the dollar's holding, there's growth without inflation in the U.S. and there's a chance of lower rates in France: What more could you ask for?" a Paris trader said.

Shares in French telecommuncations firm Alcatel Alsthom soared almost nine percent after it said it expected profits of roughly 2.5 billion francs ($451.6 million) in 1996, dealers said. The shares had risen 40 francs to 493 by 1115 GMT after hitting a high of 497.7 francs, just off its high for the year of 500 francs.
German shares jumped in early dealings as the DAX index hurdled the 3,000 point level amid prospects for further gains, traders said.
DAX heavyweight Allianz AG rose some five percent to a new record high of 3,085 marks after Goldman Sachs raised its rating on the German insurer.
In currencies, the dollar was trading steadily against the mark and yen by midday in Europe, with the market trying to find its feet after recent hectic ups and downs.

The market was using an influential Japanese official's comment that Tokyo would intervene in the market when the timing was effective -- a remark that drove dollar/yen down overnight --- as an opportunity to consolidate, traders and analysts said.

"The dollar came off quite a bit in Tokyo. Certainly Europe seemed unhappy with that level... and it's been nudging higher," said Pat Magill, head of corporate trading at Daiwa Europe. CURRENCIES AT 1200 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.6405 marks and 121.70 yen compared with late Wednesday's European levels of 1.6428 marks and 121.99 yen.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1200 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE 100 index of leading shares was up 12.8 points, or 0.3 percent, at 4,220.3.
PARIS - The CAC-40 share index was up 31.26 points, or 1.27 percent, at 2,496.27.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 12.35 points, or 0.41 percent, at 3,011.55.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $349.30 after closing on Wednesday at $351.05. Little was preventing gold from re-testing last week's low of $346 an ounce -- the lowest gold has been since September 1993.
